Consistency, not sequence: a stat that landed in at least 8 of the team's last 10 games — 8/10, 9/10 or 10/10. A team that won 8 of 10 but lost the last two shows up here and not in Streaks; a team on a 3-game run that has only hit 3 times in 10 shows up in Streaks only. ★ marks the selections that satisfy both — a live streak and an 8-in-10 hit rate — and those carry the star in the Streaks list as well. Every market is analysed, and where a team has fewer than ten games on file the card states the real denominator (9/9, 8/8) instead of pretending it has ten.

Runs most likely to continue, weighted towards the strongest competitions. Confidence is the modelled chance the run survives the next match; break-even is the minimum price worth taking (1 ÷ probability).
Long-running selections the market should price generously. Higher odds mean lower probability — treat these as value, not bankers.
Three independent tickets built from every sport's streak model. A ticket takes the strongest legs available, so it may mix sports — or end up all football, all basketball, whatever the runs say that day. Every ticket carries at least 15 legs, the minimum SportyBet's Flexi option wants, with max 5 losses as the insurance line. Only markets SportyBet accepts on a Flexi slip are used — favourites/1X2, over–under goals, both teams to score, corners, bookings, shots on target and handicaps — so the stat markets it blocks (match shots, throw-ins, fouls, tackles, offsides) never appear. No team appears twice on one ticket and the day's matches are shared out between the three tickets, so they do not cannibalise each other (a second leg from the same match is marked in the table when it is needed to reach 15). Every leg kicks off inside the next 24 hours: the day's stake settles and rolls into tomorrow, which is what makes the compounding work. Every leg is priced at 1.50 or better. Only place a leg if SportyBet's price is at or above its break-even — that is what keeps the ticket value-positive. The Flexi figures are arithmetic on the modelled prices, not SportyBet's internal split, so check their calculator before staking.
